doc: Cloud Security Alliance — Agentic AI Threat Modeling Framework: MAESTRO
title: Foundation Models
summary: The layer of core AI models such as large language models; threats at this layer concern the model itself, including its training, weights and behaviour.
note: Layer names verified 2026-09-10 against the CSA article of 6 February 2025; used as a threat-modelling reference, not a regulatory requirement.

doc: Cloud Security Alliance — Agentic AI Threat Modeling Framework: MAESTRO
title: Data Operations
summary: The layer covering data processing, storage and retrieval pipelines, including RAG stores; threats concern data poisoning, leakage and integrity.
note: Layer names verified 2026-09-10 against the CSA article of 6 February 2025.

doc: Cloud Security Alliance — Agentic AI Threat Modeling Framework: MAESTRO
title: Agent Frameworks
summary: The layer of tools and frameworks used to build agents, including orchestration, tool interfaces and plug-in mechanisms.
note: Layer names verified 2026-09-10 against the CSA article of 6 February 2025.

doc: Cloud Security Alliance — Agentic AI Threat Modeling Framework: MAESTRO
title: Deployment and Infrastructure
summary: The layer of cloud or on-premises hosting on which agents run, including compute, network and identity infrastructure.
note: Layer names verified 2026-09-10 against the CSA article of 6 February 2025.

doc: Cloud Security Alliance — Agentic AI Threat Modeling Framework: MAESTRO
title: Evaluation and Observability
summary: The layer covering monitoring, evaluation and performance assessment of agents, including traces, metrics and drift detection.
note: Layer names verified 2026-09-10 against the CSA article of 6 February 2025.

doc: Cloud Security Alliance — Agentic AI Threat Modeling Framework: MAESTRO
title: Security and Compliance (cross-cutting layer)
summary: The security and governance layer of the MAESTRO framework. CSA describes it as cutting across all other layers rather than sitting between L5 and L7, so a component is assigned to L1-L5 or L7 and the L6 concerns are attached to it — never instead of it.
note: Layer names verified 2026-09-10 against the CSA article of 6 February 2025. Correction 2026-09-16: recorded as the vertical, cross-cutting layer. Any rule that assigns a component to exactly one layer must exclude L6.

doc: Cloud Security Alliance — Agentic AI Threat Modeling Framework: MAESTRO
title: Agent Ecosystem
summary: The top layer where agents interface with marketplaces, applications, tools and users; threats concern untrusted third-party agents and tools, delegation and trust boundaries in the ecosystem.
note: Layer names verified 2026-09-10 against the CSA article of 6 February 2025; the framework also describes cross-layer threats such as supply chain attacks and lateral movement.
